detail: Transcribed 2026-09-02 from tactic-mainqa-wsl-host-activation (git archive holds the full node; serves strategy-owned-orchestration). Park reason: needs on-box nixos-rebuild switch on the actual WSL hardware plus Windows interop — not automatable; one on-box sweep around a single `sudo nixos-rebuild switch` covers all items; migrated 2026-07-05 from the legacy gh main-qa office-hours queue. Checklist: (1) Atomic activation (was 2647) — one sudo nixos-rebuild switch activates system and home-manager profile together, and no standalone home-manager switch entry point remains. (2) Standalone profile retired (was 2648) — the standalone home-manager profile no longer activates, no dotfile is double-managed, and the integrated module is the sole source of truth. (3) backupFileExtension (was 2649) — a pre-existing unmanaged file at a home-manager-managed path is preserved as <file>.backup and activation completes instead of aborting on the collision. (4) Linger keeps the mux server alive (was 2650) — with users.users.n8.linger = true, after logout/login `systemctl --user status wezterm-mux-server` is active with no manual restart and `loginctl show-user n8` shows Linger=yes. (5) wezterm connect after binary upgrade (was 2651) — `wezterm connect nixos` succeeds against the lingering mux server after the switch upgrades the binary. (6) Windows profile resolution on a multi-profile host (was 2579, PR 2458) — the activation copies the wezterm config under the active Windows user profile via cmd.exe/wslpath interop, the override tier takes precedence, and fall-through works with no override. (7) Nix fidelity anchor (was 2578) — the local nix eval of wezterm-test.nix confirms the assembled activation string contains the expected tokens (CI does not run this).
subject: mainqa (author-required): Verify the WSL host home-manager integration on-box — atomic activation, retired standalone profile, backup extension, linger/mux persistence, wezterm connect and Windows profile resolution
